findings.issue: The summary identifies iteration 10 as the cap and later explicitly records that no further implementation tick may be queued, but iteration 13 subsequently changed production code and was pushed. Twelve review reports existed before this review, so this is not a numbering typo; the extended clock did not extend the unchanged iteration cap.
findings.consequence: The autonomous workflow violated its governing stop condition, and another implementation iteration would compound the violation.
findings.correction: Stop the loop after this review. Preserve the published linear history without rollback or force operations, record the deviation, and do not queue another implementation tick.

findings.criterion: 7 and cross-cutting data integrity — mandatory idempotency for Super Admin tenant creation
findings.issue: POST /v1/platform/tenants is replaySafe rather than idempotent, so definePlatformRoute accepts and executes keyless writes. Existing tests prove keyless calls succeed. Retrying a keyless request after a lost response reruns provisionTenant, whose no-slug collision path creates a random-suffixed tenant.
findings.consequence: One intended Super Admin API operation can still create two live properties with owner memberships, starter inventory, policies, and audit history.
findings.correction: Make tenant creation idempotent with a required key, update every caller/test, assert a missing key is rejected and exact-key retry replays one tenant, and add a rendered Platform-form retry/in-flight test.

findings.criterion: 7 and cross-cutting data integrity — atomic, recoverable platform idempotency
findings.issue: Reservation, business mutation, and response finalization are separate autocommit operations with no lease or reconciliation. A process/database failure after the mutation commits but before finalization leaves status=0 forever; the same key returns request_in_progress, while a new key can rerun tenant creation and create a random-suffixed duplicate.
findings.consequence: The failure window idempotency must handle can permanently strand a committed operation or duplicate a property after retry.
findings.correction: Commit durable completion/result identity atomically with each mutation, or attach a durable unique operation ID to the resource so a stale reservation can reconstruct the committed result. Add fault-injection tests for failure after business commit and prove retry returns the single resource.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 — recoverable local-auth person and owner onboarding
findings.issue: Local creation delivers its only temporary password in the first response, while replay stores temporaryPassword as null. After a committed request whose response is lost, replay returns 201 without a usable credential and the UI reports an invitation that local auth never created; local auth has no recovery path.
findings.consequence: A created person or newly created property's only owner can exist in the database but be unable to sign in.
findings.correction: Use a recoverable setup/invitation mechanism or authenticated credential setup/reset action with an explicit replay outcome, while keeping secrets out of replay storage. Test lost-response retries for tenant, member, and owner creation through successful first local sign-in.

findings.issue: The rendered join begins with a fabricated token, mounts GuestPass directly, swaps the camera, and mocks lookup/redeem. Separate API tests cover expiry/HMAC/verify_code, but no recorded execution joins a server-generated pass to the actual Share control, public bootstrap, decoded QR, and real gate validation.
findings.consequence: The complete live pass artifact and share-to-gate path remain unverified in context.
findings.correction: Issue a live pass, invoke the real Share control, open /pass at a mobile viewport, decode its QR, and perform real lookup/redeem; assert token identity, two-hour unused expiry, HMAC rejection, and stored-verify_code mismatch rejection.

findings.criterion: 3 and 4 — real camera plate scanning at check-in and check-out
findings.issue: Rendered tests replace LiveCamera with an already-decoded plate button. No recorded run executes getUserMedia, the shipped ONNX loader/decoder, a camera fixture, and responsive rendering; the real-camera script covers only check-in.
findings.consequence: Actual camera acquisition and plate decoding remain unverified in the shipped stack for check-in and check-out.
findings.correction: Run and record the 390x844 real-model fake-camera check-in story and add/run checkout coverage, asserting filled fields, checkout match, stopped tracks, versions, and a clean console.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 — complete real-stack CRUD and cross-property operations
findings.issue: Rendered CRUD tests mock every API and do not complete every entity lifecycle against persistence. Cross-property coverage is a mocked member POST; the browser script has no recorded run, is desktop-only, and omits full person/site/slot lifecycles, representative all-entity second-property writes, real regular-admin denial, and the new Platform create retry wiring.
findings.consequence: Complete single-property administration, Super Admin operations across properties, persistence, authorization boundaries, and narrow-screen usability remain unverified in context.
findings.correction: Run and record full person/site/unit/slot lifecycles plus Platform tenant-create retry through the real routed UI/API at a narrow viewport; perform all-entity second-property operations as Super Admin and prove regular-admin server denial.
